clue.text: War planes contain about 51 incendiaries

indicators.note: the war planes contain, i.e. hold within them, the next two pieces

parts.note: fighters are military aircraft built for air combat
re is Latin-derived for 'concerning, about'
LI is 51 in Roman numerals (L = 50, I = 1)

explanation.surface: Military aircraft carrying a load of firebombs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'War planes' reads as the definition's partner in a battle picture; 'contain' is the container signal, and 51 is a Roman numeral.
explanation.definitionFit: Firelighters are blocks used to kindle a fire, so they are incendiary materials.

clue.text: Happen as a result of nuclear war

definitions.meaning: an old way of saying come about or occur
the radioactive dust that settles after a nuclear explosion

explanation.definitionFit: Things 'fall out' when they occur, and radioactive debris descending after an atomic blast bears the same name.

clue.text: Plunder loaded'?

definitions.meaning: to plunder is to ransack or rob
a gun that may be loaded with a cartridge

explanation.definitionFit: To ransack a drawer is to rifle it, and a rifle is a firearm that can be loaded.

clue.text: European design in the Italian and German context -

indicators.note: the design goes in the context made by the two articles

parts.note: la is Italian for 'the' (feminine)
der is German for 'the', the article implied by 'the' carried over
a plan is a design

explanation.surface: A continental scheme set among Italian and German concerns.
explanation.walkthrough: One 'the' serves both languages, and 'in ... context' (con-text, with text around) signals that the design sits inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A Laplander is someone from Lapland in northern Scandinavia, so a European.

clue.text: A single easy part song

annotationWithheld.why: 'A single easy part song' (4) for GLEE: 'part song' defines it but no parse of 'A single easy' gives letters of GLEE, and no source gives the wordplay

clue.text: Late leaver ?

parts.note: looks like someone slow to go home, but means a person who, now deceased, has left property by will

explanation.walkthrough: 'Late' means dead, not tardy; 'leaver' is one who leaves a bequest.
explanation.definitionFit: A testator is a person who has made a will, leaving goods to heirs at death.

clue.text: Just panic, losing head

indicators.note: the panic word loses its head, meaning its opening letter is dropped

parts.note: fright is sudden fear, panic

explanation.surface: Simply panicking and losing control.
explanation.walkthrough: 'losing head' removes F from FRIGHT.
explanation.definitionFit: Just and right both mean fair and morally proper.

clue.text: Learned people settled form of a rite

parts.note: a bird that has settled on a branch has lit there

indicators.note: a form of something is a new shape of it, so the letters of a rite take a new order

explanation.surface: Scholars agreed on how a ceremony should go.
explanation.walkthrough: 'settled' is the past of alight, as a bird lands; 'form of' is the anagram signal on the last two words.
explanation.definitionFit: The literati are well-read, educated people interested in literature.

clue.text: Sitting with an Irishman before church

indicators.note: the Irishman's name comes before the church abbreviation

parts.note: Sean is a common Irish man's name
CE stands for the Church of England

explanation.surface: A session in which an Irishman takes his place ahead of a church.
explanation.definitionFit: A seance is a meeting of people seeking contact with the dead, a sitting in that sense.

clue.text: They're entitled to look closely into various files

indicators.note: one piece goes into the other, so the look-closely word sits inside the shuffled letters
various suggests a varied arrangement, so the letters of files are rearranged

parts.note: to peer is to look closely at something

explanation.surface: People with a right to inspect assorted dossiers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'entitled' means holding a title, not deserving; 'various' is the anagram signal and 'into' the container.
explanation.definitionFit: Life peers hold titles in the House of Lords for their lifetime, so they carry a title.

clue.text: Airmen are powerless to do it

definitions.text: Airmen are powerless to do it

parts.words: Airmen are powerless to do it
parts.note: reads like a complaint about helpless pilots, but describes the motorless flight of pilots of unpowered aircraft

explanation.walkthrough: 'powerless' sounds like helplessness; it means without an engine, as in a sailplane.
explanation.definitionFit: Unpowered flight on air currents is the motion a sailplane makes.

clue.text: Nothing to spare, possibly, for entertainments

parts.note: nothing is zero, shaped like the letter O

indicators.note: possibly suggests another possible arrangement of the letters of spare

explanation.surface: Having no surplus cash, perhaps, for a night out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nothing to spare' reads as being broke; 'possibly' is the anagram signal on spare alone.
explanation.definitionFit: Operas are staged musical dramas put on as public entertainment.

clue.text: Printer's beginning with articles on a temple

indicators.note: the beginning of the word printer's is its opening letter

parts.note: an is the indefinite article in English grammar
the is the definite article in English grammar
taken as written

explanation.surface: A printer starting with some items for a place of worship.
explanation.walkthrough: The single word 'articles' supplies both the indefinite and the definite article in turn.
explanation.definitionFit: The Pantheon in Rome is an ancient temple to all the gods.

clue.text: Attacking speech one got in exchange

indicators.note: one piece gets into the other, so the letter for one goes inside the exchange word

parts.note: trade is the exchange of goods
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Someone took verbal abuse in a swap.
explanation.walkthrough: 'got in' puts I inside TRADE.
explanation.definitionFit: A tirade is a long angry harangue directed at someone.

clue.text: Rose can be so incoherent

definitions.meaning: a climbing rose with long trailing stems is described by this word

explanation.definitionFit: A rambler is a trailing climbing rose, and speech that wanders from point to point lacks coherence.

clue.text: Assembly for study gets stuck

parts.note: to con is an old word meaning to study or learn
clave is the archaic past tense of cleave in the sense of adhere, so it means stuck

explanation.surface: A student meeting that gets bogged down.
explanation.walkthrough: CLAVE is the old past tense of cleave (stick fast), as in the Bible's 'clave unto'.
explanation.definitionFit: A conclave is a private gathering, famously the cardinals meeting to elect a pope.

clue.text: Creature busily employed on Joseph's coat?

definitions.text: Creature busily employed on Joseph's coat?

parts.words: Creature busily employed on Joseph's coat?
parts.note: a lizard that changes its colour to match its background would be kept hard at work on Joseph's many-coloured garment

explanation.walkthrough: Joseph's coat of many colours is from the Bible's Genesis story.
explanation.definitionFit: A colour-changing lizard matching a multicoloured background would never rest.

clue.text: Hero's evergreen address to beloved

parts.note: O is the vocative used when addressing someone, as in 'O Romeo'
Leander was the lover of Hero in Greek myth, swimming the Hellespont to reach her

explanation.surface: A heroine's tender words to her sweetheart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hero' is not a brave person but the priestess Hero of Greek myth; her call to her beloved would begin 'O'.
explanation.definitionFit: The oleander is a poisonous Mediterranean shrub that keeps its leaves all year.

clue.text: Revolutionary vehicles returned empty of late

definitions.text: Revolutionary vehicles returned empty of late

parts.words: Revolutionary vehicles returned empty of late
parts.note: the carts that took condemned prisoners to the guillotine in the French Revolution came back with nobody aboard

explanation.walkthrough: 'Revolutionary' means of the French Revolution, and 'of late' means of the recently deceased, not recently.
explanation.definitionFit: Tumbrils were open carts that carried victims to execution during the Terror.

clue.text: Medicinal decoction mixed in East

indicators.note: mixed suggests the letters of in East are stirred into a new order

explanation.surface: A healing brew blended in the Orient.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mixed' rearranges IN EAST.
explanation.definitionFit: A tisane is a herbal infusion drunk for its soothing or healing properties.

clue.text: Little quarrel about a red leader in the list

indicators.note: the quarrel word goes about, i.e. around, the next pieces

parts.note: a tiff is a petty squabble

indicators.note: the leader of the word red is its first letter

explanation.surface: A minor row over a communist at the head of the roll.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts A and R (red's leader) inside TIFF.
explanation.definitionFit: A tariff is a schedule of charges or duties, a price list.

clue.text: Splendid supporter in the field

parts.note: fine means splendid or excellent
a leg supports a body or table

explanation.surface: A great backer out on the pitch.
explanation.walkthrough: FINE LEG is a cricket fielding position behind the batsman on the leg side, hence 'in the field'.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a cricket fielding position, a place occupied by a fielder.

clue.text: He died dramatically, taking drink on board with a chap

indicators.note: the steamship letters are taking in, i.e. holding, the drink

parts.note: SS stands for steamship, so being on board is being in SS
ale is a kind of beer
a chap is a man

explanation.surface: A man met a theatrical death after taking a drink aboard ship with a companion.
explanation.walkthrough: Arthur Miller's play Death of a Salesman: its hero dies on stage. 'taking' is the container signal, and 'on board' is the usual steamship pair.
explanation.definitionFit: Willy Loman, the travelling seller in Arthur Miller's play, dies at its end, so he died in drama.

clue.text: Fashion is an eyesore, but many appear in it

indicators.note: the many appear in the eyesore word, so its letter goes inside it

parts.note: a stye is a sore swelling on the eyelid, literally an eye sore
L is the Roman numeral for fifty, a large number

explanation.surface: A trend that is ugly, though plenty of people are seen wearing it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'eyesore' is literal: a STYE on the eyelid. 'appear in' puts L inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Style is a distinctive manner, especially in dress, the same as a fashion.

clue.text: Composer heard from Goethe?

definitions.meaning: Sir Edward ... wrote light operas such as Merrie England
the language the poet Goethe spoke and wrote

explanation.surface: A musician whose name sounded in the speech of a great poet.
explanation.definitionFit: Edward German was an English composer, and the poet Goethe's tongue was the language of Germany.

clue.text: African people like to put in a month abroad

indicators.note: the like word is put in the foreign month

parts.note: mai is French for May, a month in a foreign language
as means like, in the manner of

explanation.surface: Africans wanting to visit for a month overseas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'abroad' signals a foreign word, here the French name of a month; 'to put in' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: The Masai are a pastoral people of Kenya and Tanzania.

clue.text: Luminary's head turned by this Russian VIP

indicators.note: the head, the first two letters of the luminary word, is turned round

parts.note: a star is a luminary, a celestial body that gives light

explanation.surface: A famous figure turns his head toward an important Russian.
explanation.walkthrough: 'head turned' swaps the first two letters of STAR, giving TS first.
explanation.definitionFit: The tsar was the emperor of Russia, its most important person.

clue.text: Domestic job for girl in : Empire State

parts.note: Nan is a girl's name, short for Ann
the Empire State is New York, abbreviated NY

explanation.surface: Work in the home for a young woman in New York.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Empire State' is New York's nickname, and 'in' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A nanny is a woman employed to look after children in a household.

clue.text: Press dial for scatter effect

indicators.note: to scatter something is to throw its parts about, so the letters are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: Pushing a button to spray things about.
explanation.walkthrough: 'scatter' rearranges the nine letters of PRESS DIAL, and the whole clue also describes the result.
explanation.definitionFit: Dispersal is the spreading out of things over a wide area, the result of scattering.

clue.text: Hamlet's mother found his rebuke so agonizing

definitions.text: Hamlet's mother found his rebuke so agonizing

parts.words: Hamlet's mother found his rebuke so agonizing
parts.note: Queen Gertrude tells her son after his reproaches in the closet scene that he has cleft her heart in twain

explanation.walkthrough: In Shakespeare's play Gertrude says 'O Hamlet, thou hast cleft my heart in twain', so his words split her heart.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that tears at the heart causes deep distress, so it is agonizing.
